newsitem.title: SPAIN: GOLF-JAMES LEAD BY TWO AT HALFWAY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-JAMES LEAD BY TWO AT HALFWAY.

text.p: English Ryder Cup veteran Mark James opened a two-shot lead in the second round of the Spanish Open on Friday, but Spain's comeback man Jose Maria Olazabal captured the imagination with a hole in one.
James, looking for an eighth Ryder Cup appearance in the match against the United States at Valderrama in September, posted a four-under-par 68 to move to 135, nine under.
He is two strokes ahead of two bright young European Tour prospects, 24-year-old Englishman Lee Westwood and Denmark's Thomas Bjorn, as well as another Englishman, Roger Chapman.
They are in turn a further shot in front of Argentine Eduardo Romero, Dutchman Rolf Muntz and another Englishman, Iain Pyman, a former British Amateur champion.

Olazabal, the Turespana Masters winner in Europe only a month ago, continued his comeback after foot problems kept him out of the game for 18 months by finishing on 140 after a 71 playing alongside Australian Greg Norman, who is one better after a 70.

The Australian was so delighted to watch Olazabal's third ace as a professional, his fifth altogether, that he urged the tournament promoter to "give him a car, too. He deserves it for a beautiful shot."
He knew Olazabal's shot with a seven iron at the 178-yard 17th had earned him nothing because compatriot Jose Rozadilla had already aced there earlier in the day.
Olazabal, who holed a mammoth 60-foot putt for birdie directly before his ace, has never won a prize for a hole-in-one.
"It was a great feeling to see the ball going into the hole," Olazabal said. "And it doesn't matter about the car. Good luck to Rozadilla.

"The shot and the big putt just before it helped me get into a good position only five behind the leader and if I can put together two good rounds at the weekend I still have a chance of winning again."
James, coming out of a year-long slump, stands in his way.

The 43-year-old Englishman is not making the current Ryder Cup campaign a special case. "I'm not approaching this year any differently to any other because it is Ryder Cup year," said James, "even though our 1995 win was the highlight of my career."

Ryder Cup captain Severiano Ballesteros made his first cut of the year in seven starts despite slipping to a 73 and one-under, good enough by a stroke for the weekend. Ballesteros sacked his fourth caddie in two years directly after qualifying.

First round leaders Alex Cejka of Germany and defending champion Padraig Harrington went back into the pack, Cejka on 139 after a 73 and the Irishman only 142 following a 76 which included a lost-ball double-bogey at his second hole.
